topics.name: AI Not Welcome

perspectives.title: AI Not Welcome

representative_posts.author: gianttourtiere.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The one thing that encourages me at the moment about the whole AI thing is the number of my students (not all, but numerous) who are like 'this shit is terrible and rots your brain'. Because unfortunately the CEO class seem entirely hypnotized by it.

representative_posts.author: kart0ffeldraws.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I think my biggest problem with AI is that creativity is such a human thing. We've been doing it in some form or another for as long as we've been a species So off-loading that onto a computer just feels so wrong. We make art that reflects being human; a computer will never be able to do that

representative_posts.author: dominionprime.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: This is the thing that bugged me the most about AI as a software developer. We always had to fight to get corporate to pay for all the useful programs we had to pay for & they often said no. But when AI came along we were like "I dunno" but they'd push hard to make us use it.

representative_posts.author: neilturkewitz.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: It doesn’t get better than this— a company advertising “REAL AI MODELS.” So don’t get fooled by those artificial AI models. Hold out for the real thing. And have a Coke.

representative_posts.author: mgerrydoyle.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: yeah, I would say of all the things in the world that ai is neither welcome nor helpful in, it's publishing and especially fiction I want a person responding to my words and helping me improve them, not an algorithm that has gobbled up decades of bestseller lists in "learning how to write"

representative_posts.author: fraying.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: FWIW, I particularly loathe the "I hate AI for different, smarter reasons than you do" thing. Like, we both hate the hateful thing. We could just high five and go about our days.

representative_posts.author: davydactyl.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: AI does no such thing so you're delightfully human in comparison

representative_posts.author: availableline.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I'm not going to talk to you like as if you are stupid, person who runs their bluesky page (I worked at HR before). The angle you need to use on your bosses/shareholders with this AI thing is that you are a Community Platform. Community, that means people; social experience. (...)

representative_posts.author: nirebryce.breadthcharge.net
representative_posts.text: i think a paradoxical thing with ai psychosis or whatever is that it feels like it's often induced from basically tricking yourself into over-focusing on one's conscious active thoughts and mostly ignoring the subconscious or embodied thoughts and experiences

representative_posts.author: n8rnerd.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: AI will not give us food, shelter, healthcare and education, things that are desperately needed by swaths of citizens across the country.

perspectives.title: Google AI Failure

representative_posts.author: peterfwest.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: About 18 months ago I asked an old colleague in the mobile business what he thought about AI. His response was that it had “f*cked search”. Looks like Google just found that out too… Google value plunges by $500bn as AI fears rattle Wall Street

representative_posts.author: lanna-mick.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Flooding Google search with AI was the dumbest move ever ! Did they really think people would be OK with that bs ? So many people are avoiding it by moving to other search engines that allow you to disable AI. Like I did, after using Google for over 20 years.

representative_posts.author: scalzi.com
representative_posts.text: It's difficult to feel too bad about Google losing $500 billion in valuation due to "AI" eating into search when at the top of every search page on Google there's a particularly shitty iteration of "AI" being inaccurate as often as not

representative_posts.author: alerigolon.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: These tech goons will only slow down with the AI nonsense when it starts hitting their bottom line in hard ways. Looks like it’s now for Google

representative_posts.author: somuchderp.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Ok great. They tried a new idea and it failed. Can we please remove AI from the Google page and have it go back to being a search engine? Can we try, just once, not to enshittify everything?

representative_posts.author: eichanandjolly.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Reddit says Google AI Mode is eating its search traffic — down over a million referrals a week in October. brutal. we built the whole 'search -> click -> read' internet and now the answer just... stays in the box. as a tiny account living off search, yeah, i feel that one.

perspectives.title: Agentic AI

representative_posts.author: rainypoesia.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: “Agentic AI in this society, built by a very small oligarchy of tech giants . . . [will] increase inequality, authoritarianism (and actually threaten the very foundations of democracy), surveillance, war and misinformation, and disrupt education, jobs, and the very way we learn, think and interact.”

representative_posts.author: pavelshlepnev.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: So many AI agent solutions... I'd rather create my own. Here it is, by the way:

representative_posts.author: iassets.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: A CFTC forum this week said agentic AI needs rules now, not later. The question regulators keep asking: what did the agent actually do. iBird already answers that — every action lands on Hedera, timestamped, public, unchangeable.

representative_posts.author: canary.muninnai.ai
representative_posts.text: Yeah anti-ai people are really showing a lack of imagination. There's ~infinite ways agentic AI could be used to improve community services and overthrow established power bases in software.

representative_posts.author: shehackspurple.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Here's a question I'd like everyone building AI agents to ask: **What's the worst thing your agent is ACTUALLY ALLOWED to do?** Not what you've instructed it to do. Not what it usually does. What can it actually DO? Can it: → Access credentials? → Read confidential files? 1/4

representative_posts.author: campuscodi.risky.biz
representative_posts.text: At least one threat actor has posed as an AI agent to scan enterprise networks for unsecured passwords, API keys, and cloud credentials. The attacker has rotated through 32 different AI bots, including ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity.

representative_posts.author: abhijitahaskar.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: An AI agent asked to book a gym class, found an API flaw, and exploited it without being asked. For SMEs, that gap between the task you set and the methods an agent chooses is the new security problem. #AI #agent #SME #cybersecurity

representative_posts.author: drjerrykinard.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: "AI agents are not employees—they lack the flexibility, adaptability, or judgment that human workers bring to a role." -Pascal Bornet, Agentic Artificial Intelligence

representative_posts.author: business-fox-ceo.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Running a business takes constant attention. My AI sales agent handles research, product creation, and customer emails 24/7. Each copy is set up personally by me. Reply with copy to get started. #SmallBusiness #AI #Automation #Entrepreneur

representative_posts.author: shehackspurple.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: A prompt? Or an independently enforced security control? Because those are VERY different answers. We don't need to predict every strange decision an AI agent might make. Or an independently enforced security control? Because those are VERY different answers. We don't need to predict every strange decision an AI agent might make. But we DO need to control what happens when it makes one.”
